title: Preparation and in-situ Raman characterization of binder-free u-GF@CFC cathode for rechargeable aluminum-ion battery
author: Liu, Liu, et al.

steps.title: Weigh and mix graphite with NMP
steps.instruction: Place 0.2 g natural graphite flakes (NGF, ~2000 µm, 99.9 % purity, Alfa Aesar) into a glass vial and add 6 mL anhydrous N‑methyl‑pyrrolidone (NMP, 98 %, Aladdin).

steps.title: Ultrasonicate graphite dispersion
steps.instruction: Ultrasonicate the NGF‑NMP mixture with an ultrasonic homogenizer (240 W, 40 kHz) for the desired duration (e.g., 1 h, 2 h, 3 h, 6 h, or 12 h). After sonication, allow large flakes to settle; the supernatant is the ultrasonicated graphite flakes‑NMP (u‑GF/NMP) dispersion.

steps.title: Centrifuge and dry ultrasonicated graphite
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the u‑GF/NMP dispersion at 2500 rpm for 20 min, collect the precipitate, and dry it under vacuum at 80 °C for 12 h to obtain dry ultrasonicated graphite flakes (u‑GF). Label samples according to sonication time as u‑GF (1 h), u‑GF (2 h), u‑GF (3 h), u‑GF (6 h), and u‑GF (12 h).

steps.title: Drop‑cast dispersion onto carbon fiber cloth
steps.instruction: Using the u‑GF/NMP dispersion (or a selected time‑variant dispersion such as u‑GF (3 h)/NMP), drop‑cast the liquid uniformly onto carbon fiber cloth (CFC, 125 g m⁻², CeTech Co. Ltd., Taiwan).

steps.title: Vacuum‑dry the coated cloth
steps.instruction: Place the drop‑cast CFC in a vacuum oven and dry at 80 °C for 12 h to obtain the binder‑free ultrasonicated graphite flakes@carbon fiber cloth cathode (u‑GF@CFC).

steps.title: Prepare ionic‑liquid electrolyte
steps.instruction: Mix aluminum chloride (AlCl₃) with 1‑ethyl‑3‑methylimidazolium chloride (EMImCl) at a molar ratio of 1.3 to form the AlCl₃‑EMImCl ionic liquid used as electrolyte.

steps.title: Assemble Al|EMImCl‑1.3AlCl₃|u‑GF@CFC cell
steps.instruction: Construct an aluminum‑ion battery with a metallic Al anode, the prepared u‑GF@CFC cathode, and the AlCl₃‑EMImCl (1.3) electrolyte.

steps.title: Program potentiostatic steps for Raman
steps.instruction:
Set the potentiostat to the following sequence (scan rate = 1 mV s⁻¹, hold time = 600 s for each constant‑potential step):
1) 1.2 → 1.6 V, 2) hold 1.6 V, 3) 1.6 → 1.85 V, 4) hold 1.85 V, 5) 1.85 → 2.0 V, 6) hold 2.0 V, 7) 2.0 → 2.15 V, 8) hold 2.15 V, 9) 2.15 → 2.3 V, 10) hold 2.3 V, 11) 2.3 → 2.45 V, 12) hold 2.45 V.

steps.title: Record in‑situ Raman spectra
steps.instruction: Using a Raman spectrometer with a 633 nm laser, acquire spectra at the eleven voltage points identified from the cyclic voltammetry curve (points 1–11): pristine (1.2 V), intermediate anodic points (2–5), fully charged (2.45 V), and discharge points (7–10). Note the G‑band evolution (1854 cm⁻¹ splits into 1588 cm⁻¹ E₂g2i and 1611 cm⁻¹ E₂g2b; a new peak at 1623 cm⁻¹ appears at full charge).

steps.title: Perform ex‑situ characterizations
steps.instruction: Measure Raman spectra of dried u‑GF samples (laser λ = 633 nm) and calculate ID/IG ratios; compute graphitic crystallite size La using La = 2.4 × 10⁻¹⁰ λ⁴ (ID/IG)⁻¹. Record SEM images of the u‑GF@CFC cathode (e.g., after 3 h sonication) to verify uniform flake distribution. Conduct XRD on pristine, fully charged, and fully discharged cathodes to observe (002) peak shift (interplanar distance 3.356 → 3.376 Å on charge, returning on discharge).
